instructions: Put the 1.5 lb ribs in a large soup pot and add cold water until they're just covered. Bring it to a boil over high heat and let it bubble for 10 minutes. Grey foam will rise to the top.
Drain the ribs into a colander and throw away the water. Rinse the ribs and the pot so no foam is left.
Put the ribs back in the pot and add fresh water until they're just covered, about 8 cups. Peel the onion, cut it in half and add it. Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat down so it bubbles gently.
Simmer it for 1 1/2 hours. Every 30 minutes, skim off any foam or scum with a big spoon. That's what keeps the soup clear.
Meanwhile, put the 1 1/2 oz tamarind pulp in a small saucepan with 1 cup water. Bring it to a boil and simmer for about 5 minutes, mashing it with the back of a spoon, until the pulp breaks down.
Pour the tamarind through a fine sieve into a bowl. Press on the pulp and scrape the underside of the sieve so you get all of the paste. Throw away the seeds and fibers.

Peel the ginger and slice it into thin coins. Peel the elephant ear stems with a vegetable peeler and cut them on an angle into 1 inch pieces. Cut the 3 tomatoes into quarters. Rinse the bean sprouts.
Rinse the catfish and pat it dry. Cut it into 1 inch pieces and sprinkle 1/4 tsp of the salt over it.

When the pot has simmered for about an hour, rinse the 1.5 cups rice until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a pot with 2 1/4 cups water and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes, then take it off the heat and leave the lid on.
Pour the 1/4 cup fish sauce into a small bowl. Thinly slice the 2 chilies and put them in the fish sauce for the table.
When the pot has had its 1 1/2 hours, lift out the onion with a slotted spoon and throw it away. Add the pineapple with its juice and the ginger. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Slide in the catfish and simmer for 10 minutes, until it's white all the way through and flakes when you press it with a fork. Stir gently so the pieces stay whole.
Stir in the tamarind, the remaining 3/4 tsp salt and the 1 tsp sugar. Add the elephant ear stems and the tomatoes and bring it back to a boil.
Turn off the heat and stir in the bean sprouts. They'll soften in the hot soup in about a minute and still have some crunch.
Pull a handful of the rice paddy herb leaves off the stems, chop them roughly and scatter them over the soup.
Taste the soup. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the jasmine rice, with the fish sauce and chilies on the side.
method_notes: All three sour the broth with strained tamarind and fill it with catfish, pineapple, tomato, bean sprouts and a soft green vegetable, finishing with rice paddy herb. Cooking Therapy builds a long pork broth first, keeps fish sauce out of the pot and serves it on the side for dipping the catfish, and names celery as the swap if elephant ear stems are hard to find. Vicky Pham and Diversivore make it in about 30 minutes in water or stock seasoned with fish sauce, using okra, and Vicky Pham pan fries the fish in garlic oil first. This one follows the lead's pork broth and its tamarind, salt and sugar balance, with the fish sauce and chilies at the table.
